bullets.text: Q2 CR was 96.8 after April hit 98.4; May and June ran at or below 96; YTD CR reached 95.7, remaining on track toward the calendar-year 96 goal despite severe weather.

Net premiums written grew 13% and net premiums earned rose 11%; average premium increased approximately 4% for personal auto and 13% for commercial auto amid double-digit growth at a $20 billion-plus enterprise scale.

Unit sales growth and healthier retention served as primary drivers of overall growth; year-over-year policies in force rose 11% in Direct auto and Commercial Lines, 4% in Agency auto, with impressive Special Lines performance.

Extreme weather flowing from Q1 into Q2 put Progressive 'on the ropes'; however, the company outlasted the storms, absorbed climatic events, and created customer advantages through its claims response in times of need.

ASI exited commercial property by exchanging it for a Florida residential property business; the transaction supports Progressive's home-and-auto bundling strategy, where positive growth trends began developing during the quarter.

Terminated ASI quota share reinsurance agreement, generating a one-time NPW increase; Progressive's strong capital position eliminated the need for dollar-one risk sharing while retaining ASI's core excess reinsurance structure.

Commercial Lines experienced a rare combined ratio spike; management so far senses no systemic misses in past loss recognition nor a sustained frequency spike, but will closely watch the fast-growing segment's development.

Expenses presented concurrent challenges alongside new business growth, catastrophe response, and Property adjustments; however, overall expenses and expense outlook remain aligned with management's expectations.

Rapid policy growth strained organizational staffing across recruiting, training, supervision, and quality control; management maintains vigilance to avoid long-term erosion of customer service levels and brand quality.

Glenn Renwick concludes 16.5 years of shareholder reporting, passing executive commentary to Tricia; an upcoming October investor relations meeting in Cleveland will highlight Destination Era initiatives, customer marketing, and Snapshot.
